  23      Add type hints from a specified class to a base class:

  25      >>> class Foo(with_typehint(Bar)):

  27  
  28      This would add type hints from class ``Bar`` to class ``Foo``.
  29  
  30      Note that while PyCharm and Pyright (for VS Code) understand this pattern,
  31      MyPy does not. For that reason TinyDB has a MyPy plugin in
  32      ``mypy_plugin.py`` that adds support for this pattern.
  33      """

  38

  43  class LRUCache(abc.MutableMapping, Generic[K, V]):
  44      """
  45      A least-recently used (LRU) cache with a fixed cache size.
  46  
  47      This class acts as a dictionary but has a limited size. If the number of
  48      entries in the cache exceeds the cache size, the least-recently accessed
  49      entry will be discarded.
  50  
  51      This is implemented using an ``OrderedDict``. On every access the accessed
  52      entry is moved to the front by re-inserting it into the ``OrderedDict``.
  53      When adding an entry and the cache size is exceeded, the last entry will
  54      be discarded.
  55      """
  56  
  57      def __init__(self, capacity=None) -> None:
  58          self.capacity = capacity
  59          self.cache: OrderedDict[K, V] = OrderedDict()
  60  
  61      @property
  62      def lru(self) -> list[K]:
  63          return list(self.cache.keys())
  64  
  65      @property
  66      def length(self) -> int:
  67          return len(self.cache)
  68  
  69      def clear(self) -> None:
  70          self.cache.clear()
  71  
  72      def __len__(self) -> int:
  73          return self.length
  74  
  75      def __contains__(self, key: object) -> bool:
  76          return key in self.cache
  77  
  78      def __setitem__(self, key: K, value: V) -> None:
  79          self.set(key, value)
  80  
  81      def __delitem__(self, key: K) -> None:
  82          del self.cache[key]
  83  
  84      def __getitem__(self, key) -> V:
  85          value = self.cache.get(key, _missing)
  86          if value is _missing:
  87              raise KeyError(key)
  88  
  89          self.cache.move_to_end(key, last=True)
  90  
  91          return cast(V, value)
  92  
  93      def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[K]:
  94          return iter(self.cache)
  95  
  96      def get(self, key: K, default: Optional[D] = None) -> Optional[Union[V, D]]:
  97          value = self.cache.get(key, _missing)
  98  
  99          if value is not _missing:
 100              self.cache.move_to_end(key, last=True)
 101  
 102              return cast(V, value)
 103  
 104          return default
 105  
 106      def set(self, key: K, value: V):
 107          if key in self.cache:
 108              self.cache[key] = value
 109              self.cache.move_to_end(key, last=True)
 110          else:
 111              self.cache[key] = value
 112  
 113              # Check, if the cache is full and we have to remove old items
 114              # If the queue is of unlimited size, self.capacity is NaN and
 115              # x > NaN is always False in Python and the cache won't be cleared.
 116              if self.capacity is not None and self.length > self.capacity:
 117                  self.cache.popitem(last=False)

 120  class FrozenDict(dict):
 121      """
 122      An immutable dictionary.
 123  
 124      This is used to generate stable hashes for queries that contain dicts.
 125      Usually, Python dicts are not hashable because they are mutable. This
 126      class removes the mutability and implements the ``__hash__`` method.
 127      """
 128  
 129      def __hash__(self):
 130          # Calculate the has by hashing a tuple of all dict items
 131          return hash(tuple(sorted(self.items())))
 132  
 133      def _immutable(self, *args, **kws):
 134          raise TypeError('object is immutable')
 135  
 136      # Disable write access to the dict
 137      __setitem__ = _immutable
 138      __delitem__ = _immutable
 139      clear = _immutable
 140      setdefault = _immutable  # type: ignore
 141      popitem = _immutable
 142  
 143      def update(self, e=None, **f):
 144          raise TypeError('object is immutable')
 145  
 146      def pop(self, k, d=None):
 147          raise TypeError('object is immutable')
 148  
 149  
 150  def freeze(obj):
 151      """
 152      Freeze an object by making it immutable and thus hashable.
 153      """
 154      if isinstance(obj, dict):
 155          # Transform dicts into ``FrozenDict``s
 156          return FrozenDict((k, freeze(v)) for k, v in obj.items())
 157      elif isinstance(obj, list):
 158          # Transform lists into tuples
 159          return tuple(freeze(el) for el in obj)
 160      elif isinstance(obj, tuple):
 161          # Freeze tuple elements too, so a nested dict/list inside an
 162          # already-tuple arg (e.g. Query.test's *args) is still hashable
 163          return tuple(freeze(el) for el in obj)
 164      elif isinstance(obj, set):
 165          # Transform sets into ``frozenset``s
 166          return frozenset(obj)
 167      else:
 168          # Don't handle all other objects
 169          return obj
